knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle 2 x - 3 y,\,3 z,\,- y + 3 z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle - u^{2},\,2 u^{2} - v^{2},\,v^{2}\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ in the direction of $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D ?\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You may use $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\left\langle 8 u v,\,4 u v,\,4 u v\right\rangle$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. Use the supplied cross product:

$$
\mathbf N=\left\langle 8 u v,\,4 u v,\,4 u v\right\rangle.
$$

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=- u^{2}$, $y=2 u^{2} - v^{2}$, $z=v^{2}$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle - 8 u^{2} + 3 v^{2},\,3 v^{2},\,- 2 u^{2} + 4 v^{2}\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(- 8 u^{2} + 3 v^{2}\right)\left(8 u v\right) \\  & =- 64 u^{3} v + 24 u v^{3} \\ T_{y} & =\left(3 v^{2}\right)\left(4 u v\right) \\  & =12 u v^{3} \\ T_{z} & =\left(- 2 u^{2} + 4 v^{2}\right)\left(4 u v\right) \\  & =- 8 u^{3} v + 16 u v^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =- 72 u^{3} v + 52 u v^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(- 72 u^{3} v + 52 u v^{3}\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle x z,\,2 y,\,3 x z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle u,\,u v,\,v\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ in the direction of $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D ?\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You may use $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\left\langle v,\,-1,\,u\right\rangle$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. Use the supplied cross product:

$$
\mathbf N=\left\langle v,\,-1,\,u\right\rangle.
$$

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=u$, $y=u v$, $z=v$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle u v,\,2 u v,\,3 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(u v\right)\left(v\right) \\  & =u v^{2} \\ T_{y} & =\left(2 u v\right)\left(-1\right) \\  & =- 2 u v \\ T_{z} & =\left(3 u v\right)\left(u\right) \\  & =3 u^{2} v\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =3 u^{2} v + u v^{2} - 2 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(3 u^{2} v + u v^{2} - 2 u v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,2\pi)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle x,\,y,\,- 3 z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle u \cos{\left(v \right)},\,u \sin{\left(v \right)},\,2 u^{2}\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ in the direction of $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D ?\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You may use $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\left\langle - 4 u^{2} \cos{\left(v \right)},\,- 4 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)},\,u\right\rangle$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. Use the supplied cross product:

$$
\mathbf N=\left\langle - 4 u^{2} \cos{\left(v \right)},\,- 4 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)},\,u\right\rangle.
$$

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=u \cos{\left(v \right)}$, $y=u \sin{\left(v \right)}$, $z=2 u^{2}$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle u \cos{\left(v \right)},\,u \sin{\left(v \right)},\,- 6 u^{2}\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(u \cos{\left(v \right)}\right)\left(- 4 u^{2} \cos{\left(v \right)}\right) \\  & =- 4 u^{3} \cos^{2}{\left(v \right)} \\ T_{y} & =\left(u \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\left(- 4 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)}\right) \\  & =- 4 u^{3} \sin^{2}{\left(v \right)} \\ T_{z} & =\left(- 6 u^{2}\right)\left(u\right) \\  & =- 6 u^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product and use $\cos^2 v+\sin^2 v=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =- 4 u^{3}(\cos^2 v+\sin^2 v)+- 6 u^{3} \\  & =- 10 u^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(- 10 u^{3}\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$
